title: Philliberto: Always Lurking, Never Crowned, Suddenly Dealing
body: Alan has been running Team Pillbert since day one of the Buckaroo Football League, and he has never changed the name or gone away. In 2023 Philly went 9-5, scored 1,499.3 points, grabbed the 2 seed and marched all the way to Buckaroo Bowl I, where Kaushal's Habibsters stopped him short of the trophy. Along the way he posted the best week of his career, a 156.2-point demolition of Sonny in Week 3. For a debut season it was nearly perfect, and the 'nearly' has followed him ever since.

Then came the slide. Team Pillbert went 6-8 in 2024, snuck in as the 4 seed and finished third, a respectable result propping up a season that also featured his worst week ever: 64.1 points against Kaushal in Week 10. The 2025 season was stranger still. Phillibert piled up 1,762.9 points, easily his highest total, yet somehow went 5-11 and limped in as the 6 seed before finishing fourth. Worse, he became the first victim of Ramon's Remains, losing 94.76-92.02 in Week 9 to a team whose manager had literally been removed from the league. That loss sits on Brucie's record with an asterisk, and on Alan's with a wince.

The rivalry chart says a lot. Randy is Alan's favorite customer at 8-5, and he also holds winning marks over Mekhi (6-4) and Ramon (6-5). Kaushal, though, is the problem he can't solve: Habib owns him 2-7 and took the Bowl I crown at his expense, which makes their matchups less of a rivalry and more of a recurring nightmare. Sonny edges him 5-6, the newcomers split him (1-0 over Jordan, 0-1 to Zoe), and his playoff record overall stands at 1-2.

As a manager, Philly used to be a man of the waiver wire and nothing else: zero trades in his first two seasons and one in 2025, while his pickups climbed from 11 to 21 to 25. In 2026 that changed completely. He has already made four trades through seven weeks, more than his first three seasons combined, plus 16 pickups. Whatever happened over the offseason, Alan has decided that the patient approach was overrated.

The early returns say he might be onto something. Team Pillbert sits at 5-2 with 817.8 points and a 17 percent shot at the title, and the league's favorite villain is back in the hunt for the one thing he has never had: a Buckaroo Bowl. Everyone else will be rooting against him. That has never seemed to slow Alan down.
